text:
Anya (Product): @channel quick heads-up — tomorrow at 10:00am PT we'll flip the hosted Stream Bridge to stable for the new multiplexed streaming + unified tool bridging flow. This is a staged onramp (canaries then regional), not a breaking change. Please read the rollout checklist and callouts below :tada:

Ravi (Eng): Nice. Are there any API changes clients need to make to opt into this?

Anya (Product): No breaking surface changes. Clients can opt-in by sending the header `X-Stream-Bridge: 1` or by adding the query flag `?bridge=stream` for a trial. Example (curl):

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "X-Stream-Bridge: 1" \
     -d '{"model":"mosaicx-lite","input":"hello","stream":true}' \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Lina (Docs): Docs PR is merged: https://git.redwood/docs/pulls/4321 — migration guide, examples for node/python, and SDK snippets are in the "stream-bridge" section. I'll push a short "what changed" snippet into quickstart today.

Samir (SRE): Operational notes: canary sequence = us-west-2 -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1. Canary window = 30m. Abort criteria: sustained p50 > 200ms or error rate delta > 1.5x baseline. Health checks will be posted automatically to #eng-oncall. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/sb-stable-onramp (please keep this pinned).

DeployBot: Scheduled deploy job created — id sb-197123. Canary start 2026-03-24T17:00:00Z. Will post live logs to this thread when it starts.

Joanne (Research): Quick model note: multiplexing batches multiple short chats; our evals on mosaicx-lite show negligible quality drift for tool-calling patterns. Cost implication: approx 3-8% compute reduction for chat-heavy workloads (depends on request length distribution). We updated quality checks in Optimize to watch for regression.

Ravi (Eng): Will function/tool-calling signing or payload shape change?

Anya (Product): Function calling interface stays identical — tool calls still use the `tools` array and `tool_call` markers. Stream Bridge coordinates multiplexing and KV cache handling under the hood. Example payload snippet: { "stream_bridge": true, "tools": [...], "input": "..." }. SDKs will surface a `bridge` option.

Samir (SRE): Fallback behavior: if bridge path reports errors or exceeds latency SLO we automatically route to legacy endpoint `/v0/stream` for that customer/route for 10m before trying bridge again. Please don't whitelist bridge-only traffic until after regional confirmation.

Lina (Docs): I'll add a "quick diff" showing old vs new request/response examples and a short troubleshooting checklist for customers (timeouts, truncated responses, tool call ordering).

Anya (Product): Action items: engineering please watch canary metrics and be ready to rollback in first 30m; docs please publish the short migration note; SRE please monitor error budget and escalate if abort threshold hit. If any post-deploy regressions surface, create an incident and tag @Samir. Thanks all — excited to get lower latencies and simpler tool integration across hosted customers :rocket:

Ravi (Eng): :thumbsup: I'll be watching the canary dashboards.

DeployBot: Canary started (job sb-197123) — logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/sb-197123/logs

Samir (SRE): Canary health at +5m: p50 120ms, errors flat. Continuing to us-east-1 in 10m.

Anya (Product): Will post a short retrospective and any follow-ups after the regional onramp completes. Ping me directly for any urgent customer escalations.

Joanne (Research): Noted — I'll keep an eye on our eval hooks for tool-calling edge cases and post any anomalies here.

Lina (Docs): Migration note published to /docs/stream-bridge and included in the release email template.

DeployBot: Canary complete: succeeded. Proceeding to regional rollout.

Samir (SRE): Regional rollout complete for us-west-2/us-east-1/eu-west-1. No aborts. Closing monitoring window in 10m.

Anya (Product): Thank you everyone — will follow up with usage numbers and cost impact in 48h.
